why: Drawing fills the lower half of each top-collar leaf with contrast while the upper/fold edge stays base cloth; photo shows navy occupying the lower diagonal band of both leaves down to the points with white along the top fold edge, matching the split direction.

Drawing puts the contrast on the upper portion of the top collar adjacent to the fold/neck with the point region left in base cloth; photo shows blue along the top fold edge of both leaves running to the back neck, with white at the collar points - inverse of the lower-part option, as required.

Drawing specifies a single narrow 1.0 cm strip running lengthwise through the middle of the top collar, interrupted at the centre-front V; photo shows one narrow slate-blue strip of roughly one-centimetre width tracking the collar mid-band on both leaves and stopping at the inner leaf corners - one strip, not an edge trim or a full panel.

Drawing marks only the 0.6 cm collar point opening edges - the two front edges forming the V from tip up to the stand - with no contrast on the outer/lower collar edge; photo shows exactly that: thin red piping on both opening edges only, outer leaf edges and points left plain white.

Drawing callout shows a 1.0 cm transverse bar set back 4 cm from the collar point opening edge, crossing the full leaf from fold to lower edge; photo shows one dark-red bar of that width crossing the leaf at roughly mid-leaf, clearly set back from the point, and mirrored on the opposite leaf.

Drawing calls for the same 1.0 cm transverse bar but only 1.5 cm back from the collar point opening edge; photo places the red bar hard against the front/point end of the leaf, distinctly closer to the tip than the 4 cm variant, so the offset ordering between the two options is preserved.

Drawing shows exactly one contrast stripe running vertically down the left edge of the front placket; photo shows a single navy stripe on one placket edge only, with the opposite placket edge plain - stripe count of one confirmed at high zoom past two buttons.

Drawing shows two parallel contrast stripes flanking both edges of the front placket; photo shows exactly two red vertical stripes, one on each placket edge, running the full length past the collar button and the next button - count of two verified, not one and not three.

Drawing traces a 0.6 cm contrast edge around the entire top collar outline - down the opening edge to the point and back along the outer/lower leaf edge toward the shoulders; photo shows continuous red edge trim on both segments of both leaves, distinguishing it correctly from the point-opening-only option.

Drawing shows a small solid 2 cm contrast triangle at each of the two collar point tips and nowhere else; photo shows one red triangular patch at each collar point tip, both leaves, with the rest of the collar plain white - shape, count and location all match.

Drawing shows dashed stitch outlines at both point areas plus No Felling Stitch, i.e. a stay permanently sewn inside. The photo shows a closed stitched stay channel consistent with a fixed stay, but also an unexplained button plus buttonhole slit on the collar leaf appearing nowhere in the drawing, which could equally read as a removable-stay opening; fixed-versus-removable cannot be settled from this frame.

The defining feature is two buttons stacked vertically on a tall rounded collar stand (both marked in red at centre front). The photo shows a standard-height band carrying a single visible button at the throat, with the second button position covered by a necktie knot; the button count that defines this option is not depicted and the visible stand reads as an ordinary one-button band rather than a tall round two-button stand.
